tagline: An offline, listen-first conversation reader where your choices bend the dialogue.
short_description: A browser-only language-learning reader with branching conversations, synchronized L1/L2 audio and text, hover glosses, and replay-one-decision mode—no server, no API keys.
long_description: You Don't Say is an interactive, listen-first conversation reader for language learners. You hear two people talking; at decision points the audio pauses and you choose what one speaker says next, guiding a linear timeline that interpolates your choices into later lines. Read and Hear are independent axes—L1, L2, both, or neither—and a third channel supplies author-written hints rather than literal translation. Hovering any word or phrase reveals an on-demand gloss. The four decisions produce eight authored lines instead of sixteen forked scripts, and afterward a one-decision replay shows how the same conversation resolves differently. Everything is a static single-page app: Supertonic TTS voices both languages with one voice identity, OPUS-MT translation runs client-side, and no network call is needed after first load. The current catalog is Spanish/English.
notes: Custom domain yds.livive.net from CNAME; GitHub Pages deploy workflow included. The README is explicitly a concept narrative and defers to docs/design D1-D7. Current authored content is Spanish/English (cafe, clothes shopping, getting there, not feeling well), delivered by a Vite + Preact + TypeScript SPA with client-side models.

how_to_play.title: 1. Pick a conversation
how_to_play.body: Choose a scene and set your language pair. Read and Hear can each be L1, L2, both, or off, so you can listen first and reveal text only when needed.

how_to_play.title: 2. Guide the dialogue
how_to_play.body: At each decision point two option cards appear. Your pick plays, joins the transcript, and sets a variable that later lines interpolate—so the story bends without forking into separate scripts.

how_to_play.title: 3. Replay the road not taken
how_to_play.body: Hover any phrase for a gloss, toggle hints off for a harder listen, and afterwards swap a single decision to hear the same conversation arrive somewhere else.
